key_insight: By treating OAM propagation as qubit evolution, the paper shows that turbulence causes structured leakage out of the logical OAM subspace, and those leakage patterns can be exploited as robust quantum features.
engineering_relevance: This provides a physics-informed way to model and diagnose turbulence-degraded optical communication links while enabling more robust feature extraction for high-dimensional quantum sensing and communication.
method: Map OAM modes to a logical-qubit representation with turbulence modeled as a noisy quantum channel.
Quantify leakage from the logical subspace as a function of turbulence strength and OAM order.
Use distributed quantum feature extraction with quantum convolutional operations to learn turbulence-robust signatures.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulations and experimental measurements showing robust feature extraction across a broad range of turbulence strengths, OAM orders, and propagation conditions.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate encoding and control of high-dimensional OAM states, so performance may be sensitive to experimental imperfections and channel mismatch.
paper_title: Structured leakage in OAM-encoded qubits revealed by distributed quantum feature extraction
